metadata.title: Anthropic just went public. Here's what SpaceX and Facebook IPOs tell us about where the stock goes next.

content.text:
Anthropic just went public. Here's what SpaceX and Facebook IPOs tell us about where the stock goes next.
History shows you may not want to get sucked into the excitement over Anthropic (ANT) now that it's past its much-hyped IPO.
The average maximum drawdown for major IPOs 12 months after their debuts, dating back to 2004, is a 55.4% drop, per data from Carson Group chief market strategist Ryan Detrick.
The award for the worst post-IPO decline goes to Circle (CRCL), with an 80.9% decline. The best is Mastercard (MA), with a 13.1% decline.
SpaceX's (SPCX) decline tallied 48.8%.
"Looking at previous major IPOs shows that a pop on Day 1 is common. But so is a massive correction at some point over the next year," Detrick said.
Shares of Anthropic dropped 13% in premarket trading on Friday as investors booked profits after a frenetic first day of trading.
Anthropic made a monster debut on Wall Street Thursday, with shares opening at $111.50 a little before noon ET, a 34% premium to the $83 IPO price.
But the AI company's stock couldn't hold on to its early gains.
The stock closed at $97.17, up 17% on the day.
That closing price gave Anthropic a market capitalization of about $1.28 trillion, or roughly $1.75 trillion on a fully diluted basis. Not bad for a company founded only five years ago, in a historic IPO that raised $81.3 billion.
